chapter.title: Grandmother’s Quilt
chapter.tagline: Measuring perimeter with border lace and calculating area with square grids
chapter.overview: Preetha and Adrit's grandmother weaves a quilt from upcycled fabric patches. She decorates the border with lace, leading children to investigate perimeter (total boundary length). By overlaying 1 cm square grids, they discover area and shapes with equal area but different boundaries.

sections.title: Decorating the Quilt Border: Perimeter
sections.subtitle: Calculating the total distance around a closed 2D shape

storyNarrative.dialogue: My quilt is 2 metres long and 1.5 metres wide. How many metres of golden lace must we buy to stitch around all four sides?

concept.heading: Perimeter of a Rectangle
concept.keyRule: Perimeter = Length + Width + Length + Width = 2 × (Length + Width). For 2m by 1.5m: 2 × (2 + 1.5) = 7 metres.

questions.prompt: What is the perimeter of a square with side length 5 cm?
questions.hint: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 5 cm.

sections.title: Grid Area: Counting 1 cm² Squares
sections.subtitle: Measuring the surface enclosed within a boundary

storyNarrative.dialogue: Adrit, place the transparent 1 cm square grid on top! If a patch covers 12 full unit squares, its area is 12 square centimetres!

concept.heading: Area by Unit Square Counting
concept.keyRule: Area is the amount of surface inside a 2D boundary, quantified in square units (cm², m²).

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 4 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its area?

sections.title: Different Shapes, Same Area
sections.subtitle: Comparing shapes with identical area but different perimeters

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look! A long 1 × 12 rectangle and a 3 × 4 rectangle both have an area of 12 cm², but the long one needs 26 cm of lace while the other needs only 14 cm!

concept.heading: Isoperimetric Independence
concept.keyRule: Shapes with the exact same area can have dramatically different perimeters.
